newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian 97/98 newsprint prices lower - Fletcher.
newsitem.headline: Australian 97/98 newsprint prices lower - Fletcher.

text.p: New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd chief executive Hugh Fletcher said on Thursday its Australian newsprint prices - fixed every June for a year - would be slightly lower in 1996/97 than in the previous year.
"Australian Newsprint Mill's (ANM) price for the next 12 months is slightly lower than the last 12 months," he told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.

Fletcher, whose Paper division this week completed its A$293 million buyout of ANM from The News Corp Ltd group, said the price was "fixed off" the current US$580 per tonne U.S. West Coast transaction price.
Fletcher said newsprint prices were increasing and the outlook was "reasonably good for further increases" but he said they remained far away from previous highs.
"I don't think we will go to US$750, it is not in the industry's interest to go that high," he said when asked where the price might be in a year's time.
"We need sustainable prices that definitely start with a six," he said.
Fletcher said he believed the company paid a "fair but reasonably full price" for ANM and its immediate challenge was to increase production out of the three mills in New Zealand and Australia.
"We would expect that most of that extra potential capacity will go into enhanced newsprints rather than newsprint and that will also require some capital expenditure," he said.
Fletcher said a second newsprint paper machine at the company's Albury plant was conditional on the conversion of capacity in the Boyer, Tasmanian plant to coated papers.
"I think a decision on Tasmania would bring with it a decision on Albury," he said, adding the company had to ascertain whether improving prices were sustainable or just an inventory cycle.
